chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

To one of his sons: 'Did you walk briskly in the valley of Muhassar?' He said, 'No.' So he ordered him to return until he walked briskly. His son said to him, 'I do not know it.' So he said to him, 'Ask the people.'
ai.seo_question: What did the Imam instruct his son to do regarding the valley of Muhassar?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the specific ritual of performing *sa'y* (brisk walking) in the valley of Muhassar, a practice rooted in the traditions of the Ahl al-Bayt. When the Imam’s son was unfamiliar with the location, the directive to 'ask the people' underscores the reliance on communal knowledge and scholarly transmission to preserve the precise details of these devotional acts.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, and someone else, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

having said to one of his<sup>asws</sup> sons: ‘Did you walk briskly in the valley of Muhassar?’ So he said, ‘No’. So he<sup>asws</sup> ordered him that he should return until he walks briskly. So his<sup>asws</sup> son said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I do not recognise it’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘Ask the people’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hafs ibn af-Bakhtariy and others who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

once asked one of his sons, ’Did you do Sa‘y (running slowly) in Wadiy Muhassar?’ He replied, ‘No, I did not do so.’ He (the Imam) commanded him to go back to perform Sa‘y (running slowly). His son said, ‘I do not know how to do it.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Ask the people how to do it.’”
